objective: Establish whether claude.ai connectors (such as the Exa connector) are usable in Claude Code outside claude.ai (local CLI, desktop, IDE), under which login and settings, and what MCP tool names they get there.
scope: Context: holyagent currently depends on the exa@claude-plugins-official plugin (hosted MCP at https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp) and denies the built-in WebSearch and WebFetch so web work goes through Exa. The plan is to drop the plugin and rely on the user's claude.ai Exa connector. In this claude.ai cloud session the connector tools are named mcp__Exa__web_search_exa and mcp__Exa__web_fetch_exa.

Questions: (1) Does Claude Code CLI/desktop load claude.ai connectors, and only with a claude.ai subscription login (not API key, Bedrock, Vertex)? Which setting or env var turns it on or off (for example ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS)? (2) What tool-name prefix do those connectors get in the local CLI versus cloud sessions? (3) With no connector available, what web tools remain if WebSearch and WebFetch are denied? (4) Can Exa's hosted MCP be added without the plugin (claude mcp add) and does it work without OAuth?
Use official Anthropic docs (code.claude.com/docs, docs.claude.com, support.claude.com) and Exa's docs; look facts up even if they seem known, since they change often.
constraints: Separate sourced facts (with URL and date) from inference.

criteria.text: Each of the four questions is answered with a cited source or stated as unverified

result:
result: Connectors do load in local CLI, IDE and Agent SDK sessions, but only under a claude.ai subscription login. They get the prefix `mcp__claude_ai_<Server>__<tool>` there. Exa's hosted MCP can be added without the plugin and works keyless. All four questions are answered below.

changed: none

checks: none run (read-only research). Sources were read with Exa search and fetch on 2026-10-29. The Claude Code docs pages carry no publish date and reflect the docs at that fetch.

blockers: none

questions:
- The exact claude.ai-side name of the Exa connector is unverified, so the final local tool names are inferred. Run `/mcp` in a local CLI session to confirm them.
- I did not read the "Disable claude.ai connectors" section in full. The setting name `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, the env var `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` and its `=false` behavior are sourced only from the settings reference, the MCP page's governing-settings text and GitHub issues.

notes:

**Q1: Do connectors load outside claude.ai, and what controls them? (sourced)**
- Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, section "Use MCP servers from claude.ai".
  - If you are logged into Claude Code with a claude.ai account, connectors you added at claude.ai/customize/connectors are automatically available.
  - `/mcp` lists them with a claude.ai indicator.
  - On Team and Enterprise plans, only admins can add them.
- The same page's "How connectors reach Claude Code" table says the fetch applies to:
  - Terminal, VS Code, JetBrains and Agent SDK sessions: Claude Code fetches the connectors from claude.ai itself.
  - Cloud sessions: the cloud host passes them in.
  - The desktop app's local and SSH sessions: the desktop app delivers them in-process.
  - Desktop WSL sessions: no row, because connectors are "still rolling out" there.
- Connectors are fetched only when the active auth is a claude.ai subscription login. They are not loaded, even after a prior `/login`, when any of these is active:
  - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `apiKeyHelper`
  - Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform (Vertex)
  - `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE` or the federation variables
  - `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token`
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/feature-availability says the same: connectors "load only when your claude.ai subscription is the active authentication method". Run `/status` to see the active auth method.
- Controls named by the docs:
  - `disableClaudeAiConnectors` (setting, any file) turns the fetch off.
  - `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` is an env var. GitHub issues #31249 and #29368 and a PR in another repo use `=false` to disable all connectors. A later comment on #20412 says `=0` also works. The unofficial turboai.dev page says it is listed in the official reference.
  - `allowAllClaudeAiMcps` (managed only) loads connectors alongside a deployed `managed-mcp.json`.
  - These three act only on the "Claude Code fetches itself" row.
- Version caveats:
  - Issue #38567 reports a fix in v2.1.83 so connectors are available in `claude -p` (print mode) when `--bare` is not used.
  - `--bare` skips MCP servers.
  - Issue #84301 is an open report of connectors not appearing in the CLI despite a connected account. Treat first-time load as something to verify.
- Precedence: a server you added in Claude Code with the same URL as a connector takes precedence, and `/mcp` shows the connector as hidden.
- Inference: Exa is not in the list of Anthropic-hosted connectors that reject local OAuth (Microsoft 365, Gmail, Google Calendar). The Exa connector should therefore load like any other, but I found no source naming Exa in this context.

**Q2: Tool-name prefix (sourced and inferred)**
- Sourced: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions says "Tools from connectors Claude Code fetches itself appear as `mcp__claude_ai_<server>__<tool>`". GitHub issue #64521 shows `mcp__claude_ai_Asana__add_comment`.
- Inferred: local CLI names for Exa would be `mcp__claude_ai_Exa__web_search_exa` and `mcp__claude_ai_Exa__web_fetch_exa`.
- The permissions page says special characters in server names become `_`. Whether the name keeps a space or case depends on the claude.ai display name, so confirm it in `/mcp`.
- Cloud sessions: the `mcp__Exa__...` names you see in this session are from observation only. The docs say the cloud host passes connectors in, but I found no doc stating the cloud prefix.
- Plugin MCP names have a third form: `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`. For the exa plugin that would be `mcp__plugin_exa_exa__web_search_exa`.
- Impact on the repo: allow and deny rules and `allowed-tools` lists are keyed on the exact name. A `mcp__Exa__*` entry will not match local `mcp__claude_ai_Exa__*` tools. A wildcard after the literal `mcp__<server>__` prefix is allowed, but the server segment must be glob-free.

**Q3: Web tools left if WebSearch and WebFetch are denied (sourced)**
- Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.
  - WebSearch's backend is not configurable; to search with another provider, "add an MCP server that exposes a search tool".
  - WebSearch is unavailable on Amazon Bedrock.
  - `WebFetch` can be turned off with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH=1` (v2.1.285 or later).
  - WebFetch can be withheld on Team and Enterprise accounts until the organization policy loads.
- With both denied and no MCP search or fetch server connected, no dedicated web tool remains.
- Inference: `Bash` with curl is still the only route, if it is permitted and the sandbox network allowlist allows it. A search-less session would fall back to that.

**Q4: Exa MCP without the plugin (sourced)**
- Source: https://exa.ai/docs/reference/exa-mcp, shown in the Exa pages. The Claude Code command is `claude mcp add --transport http exa https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`. The same command appears at https://exa.ai/docs/integrations/claude-web-desktop. The plugin route is `claude plugin install exa@claude-plugins-official`.
- The Claude Code docs (`/docs/en/mcp`) give the same `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>` syntax, with `--header` for tokens.
- Auth, per https://exa.ai/docs/get-started/exa-mcp: "No API key is required to get started."
  - Keyless: free and rate-limited. Without a key you get HTTP 429 once the free limit is hit.
  - OAuth: connect to `https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?login`.
  - API key: send the `x-api-key` header.
  - https://github.com/exa-labs/exa-mcp-server says the hosted server "works anonymously with rate limits".
- The "plugin:exa:exa requires authentication" notice in this session suggests the plugin entry uses the OAuth path. That is an observation from this session, not a doc claim.
- Name caveat: `claude mcp add ... exa` gives tool names `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` and `mcp__exa__web_fetch_exa`. Those names differ from the connector names in Q2.

**Decision for the root, from Q1 to Q4**
- The `claude_ai_` connector route only works for subscription-login users on non-cloud surfaces. It silently disappears on API key, Bedrock, Vertex, `setup-token` or `--bare`.
- Combined with denying WebSearch and WebFetch, that leaves such users with no web tools at all. A project-scoped `.mcp.json` entry with `type: http` at `https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp` (about as portable as the plugin) would not depend on login, but that choice is the root's to make.
- Any permission or `allowed-tools` text in holyagent that names the Exa tools must cover the `mcp__claude_ai_Exa__*` form.
